To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin and the insulin mimetic S597 differentially activate gene transcription in cells via the same IR (insulin) receptor, resulting in different mitogenic properties.

insulin and S-597 acting via the insulin receptor differentially affect the expression of genes involved with the mitogen-activated protein-kinase pathway, which may explain the different mitogenicity observed for these ligands.

(1) insulin and S597 activate the IR in the same way; (2) insulin and S598 activate different signalling cascades; (3) insulin and S599 activate the MAPK (p44/p42) cascade; and (4) the activation of the p44/p42 cascade leads to different gene expression profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms of insulin action, which is of fundamental interest for the understanding of the molecular basis of insulin resistance and diabetes.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the insulin and IGR-I (insulin-like receptor-1) signalling pathways, and with the development of novel insulin mimetics with potential therapeutic applications in the treatment of diabetes and other insulin-resistant states.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of the insulin and IGR (insulin growth factor receptor) mimetic and antagonistic peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin and S 597 activate the IR, but the downstream effects are different, which is consistent with their differential biological activities.
S597 is not insulin and that insulin is not S597.
insulin and insulin mimetic peptides have different biological effects on gene expression and that this difference is related to the activation of the mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin and S 597 are different agonists of the IR, and that the differences in the activation of downstream signalling cascaded are responsible for the differential mitogenic effects.
insulin and S-597 activate the IR with different kinetics and different downstream signalling cascades and that these differences result in differential gene regulation and mitogenicity.
insulin and S-597 activate the IR with the same affinity and the same in vivo potency, but with different signalling and gene expression responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of the same receptor by different agonists can have different biological effects.
the same receptor can be activated by different ligands to produce different biological responses.

, despite the high homology between insulin and S597 and despite the fact that they bind to the same receptor, they activate a different signalling network, which ultimately translates into different biological outcomes.
